resources.string: Take turns tapping the big die. Your piece hops along the numbered track, one square for each dot, and then it is the next player\'s turn.
Ropes: land at the foot of a rope and you climb up to a higher square. Look for the twisted vines with an arrow pointing up.
Slides: land at the top of a slide and down you go. The wide striped ramps have an arrow pointing down.
The first piece to reach square 100 wins. Go past 100 and you bounce back; with Exact roll to finish switched on you stay put until you roll the right number.

A player with a spare roll gets two round buttons after rolling: the check keeps the roll, the die in an arrow rolls again, once per game. Computers can fill empty seats. Same device only: there is no Nearby or Online mode.
Games like this go back to ancient India, where a board game called Moksha Patam used ladders for good deeds and snakes for bad ones.
